back: The equilibrium constant for the formation of a complex ion in a solvent from its constituent ions or molecules.
[[Cu(NH₃)₄(H₂O)₂]²⁺] / ([[Cu(H₂O)₆]²⁺][NH₃]⁴); units dm¹² mol⁻⁴; no water term.

front: Why water is left out of Kstab
back: It is the solvent, in huge excess, so its concentration is effectively constant.
Kstab = K₁ × K₂ × K₃ × …; lg Kstab = lg K₁ + lg K₂ + ….

front: Ratio of complex to aqua ion

back: The ligand that forms the complex with the larger Kstab displaces the other (for Cu²⁺: Cl⁻ < NH₃ < EDTA⁴⁻).
Polydentate ligands release several water molecules, so the number of particles and ΔS increase; ΔG is more negative and Kstab larger.
Treating heavy-metal (e.g. lead) poisoning, softening water, and binding metal ions in foods and cosmetics.
Kstab tells you where the equilibrium lies, not how fast it is reached.
